arm: Bimanual YAM arms; AgiBot Genie-1 humanoid; Unitree G1 humanoid (whole-body locomanipulation); simulated Galaxea R1 Pro
sim: Galaxea R1 Pro simulated on the BEHAVIOR suite; physics engine, timestep, and env count not stated
paper_code_mismatch: code/md is the current Isaac-GR00T main branch (N1.7 generation, commit 51d4c89f), not the N1.6 checkpoint; the repo names a separate n1d6 branch for N1.6 that was not fetched. The page states N1.6's backbone is "an internal NVIDIA Cosmos-2B VLM variant," but the repo's own changelog states the Eagle backbone (nvidia/Eagle-Block2A-2B-v2) was used through N1.6 and only replaced by Cosmos-Reason2-2B in N1.7 -- whether the page's Cosmos-2B variant is a third distinct model or the page is describing N1.7 under an N1.6 headline is not resolvable from what was fetched.
note_gaps: No success rate, trial count, or benchmark table for N1.6 vs. N1.5 is given anywhere on the page; no hand model, DoF count, observation vector, or action-space detail is given for any of the four embodiments; N1.6's own parameter count is only implied by the checkpoint name (nvidia/GR00T-N1.6-3B), never stated as text; human-video pretraining (EgoScale, 20K hours) is a code-changelog fact attributed to N1.7, not stated on the N1.6 page and not included here.
params: 3B (implied only by the checkpoint name nvidia/GR00T-N1.6-3B; not stated as text on the page)
action_head: flow-matching DiT, 32 layers (2x N1.5's 16); removes N1.5's post-VLM 4-layer adapter in favor of unfreezing the VLM's top 4 layers; predicts state-relative action chunks for most embodiments rather than absolute joint angles or EEF positions
pretrain_data: N1.5 pretraining mixture plus "several thousand hours" of additional teleoperated data from bimanual YAM arms, AgiBot Genie-1, simulated Galaxea R1 Pro (BEHAVIOR suite), and Unitree G1 whole-body locomanipulation; pretrained for 300K steps at global batch size 16384; post-training typically 10K-30K steps at batch size <=1K
dexterous_evidence: The page never names a hand model, gives a hand DoF count, or uses the word "finger"; "dexterity" appears once, generically ("requiring long-horizon reasoning, dexterity, and multi-tasking abilities", Discussion), not tied to any specific end effector. None of the four listed embodiments (YAM arms, AgiBot Genie-1, Galaxea R1 Pro, Unitree G1) is described as using a multi-fingered hand versus a parallel gripper, so this cannot be settled from the source.
